title: ARKST Single-S-Box Key-Difference Completeness
summary: For SPNs, ARKST forms a candidate key-difference space, but it remains unresolved whether the single-S-box restriction captures every alpha-admissible difference.

formal_statement.body: For an SPN, ARKST restricts each round's key-difference component $W_i$ to a difference $a_i$ that activates at most one S-box, represented as $a_i=L(c_i)$ with $\operatorname{wt}_b(c_i)\le 1$, and forms a candidate $\alpha$-admissible key-difference space from the linear combinations of the differences obtained in this way. The unresolved question is whether these single-S-box-activation differences span every $\alpha$-admissible key difference, so that the restriction is complete after taking linear combinations, even though individual $\alpha$-admissible differences may activate more than one S-box.

scope.domain: Cryptanalysis of SPN integral attacks, focusing on ARKST key-difference spaces.
parameters: a_i: a difference activating at most one S-box
c_i: the vector representing a_i under the weight-at-most-one condition
alpha-admissible key-difference space: the target space for the span claim
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the single-S-box-activation differences span every alpha-admissible key difference, making the restriction complete after taking linear combinations, even though individual alpha-admissible differences may activate more than one S-box.

citations.label: When the Wrong Key Lives On: The Key-Recovery Procedure in Integral Attacks

progress.summary: The source presents this as an explicit conjecture that activating one S-box at a time captures all existing alpha-admissible key differences. It clarifies that individual admissible differences may activate multiple S-boxes but are expected to be linear combinations of the minimal ones.
citation_labels: Christof Beierle et al., When the Wrong Key Lives On: The Key-Recovery Procedure in Integral Attacks
